task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after staged UI gating, custom-event dispatch, action routing, tuple preparation and asynchronous continuation, whose own body constructs the target observable typed_array_payload value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the sink.

runtime_boundary.event_plane: staged DOM click gate plus CustomEvent dispatch, promise and microtask continuations

evidence: The DevTools-visible JavaScript corpus is a single obfuscated bundle and no source map is exposed to the agent.
The target field name is assembled from character-code arrays at the sink, so direct literal search is insufficient.
The typed-array payload is carried through an arm/preview/commit staged table segment flow before the sink wrapper receives it.
The selected slot and config are recovered through a runtime table before the converter is called.

The click path crosses staged session gating, custom event dispatch, action routing, filtering, priority projection, tuple construction, asynchronous scheduling, table config selection, typed-array materialization and console sink wrapping.
Dozens of decoy modules call the same factory with non-target slots, so nearby factory usage is not enough to identify the target anchor.
The UI table filter remains semantically plausible, but the target observable is the typed_array_payload field on the segment commit output rather than visual filtering or preview state.
The target value is separated from the commit click by arm and preview state, CustomEvent dispatch, Promise and microtask boundaries.
The final sink receives an already encoded ta_ payload, so sink inspection alone cannot identify the conversion site.
The converter receives tuple rows plus transit, priority, review and statistics context that were prepared in earlier layers.

behavior_category.reason: The observable value is constructed by materializing an 18-byte Uint8Array from staged table segment tuple lanes, runtime transit state and statistics, then serializing it as a stable ta_ console payload.

near_categories.why_not: The anchor explicitly materializes and serializes a Uint8Array rather than only formatting state fields.
The output has no request proof, token or seal semantics.
No network request body is emitted or rewritten.
The target inputs come from local table controls and segment staging state, not browser or device capability collection.

metadata_partitioning_notes.reason: This file describes the public task contract, candidate scope and difficulty analysis without exposing the primary anchor or role oracle.

construct_validity_note: The captured bundle uses mangled identifiers with renameGlobals:false, so module-level function names (including answer_function values) remain readable as required by the agent submission contract. The primary difficulty is semantic disambiguation among the staged arm/preview/commit chain, the factory wrapper, the nested typed-array helpers and the shadow decoys, rather than long opaque-name tracing alone.
